chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs34768248
predictions: The G and A alleles do not show a reproducible TF-binding difference relevant to the disease; any association could instead reflect linkage or no causal effect.
falsified_if: A variant-dependent TF-binding difference is reproducibly detected in a relevant cellular context and is linked to altered TERT regulation.

chains.title: GABPA binding alters TERT regulation
chains.element: A putative TERT promoter-proximal regulatory element

links.claim: Hypothesis: GABPA binds the A allele more strongly than the G allele. GABPA is a literature-motivated candidate because ETS-family recruitment has been implicated at the TERT promoter; no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result for this variant was supplied, so the direction is conjectural.
Hypothesis: the variant affects a promoter-proximal cis-regulatory element controlling TERT.
Hypothesis: stronger GABPA binding on the A allele increases TERT expression.
Hypothesis: this effect occurs in glioblastoma cells; the supplied expression context does not establish GABPA occupancy or an allelic effect.
Hypothesis: altered TERT regulation could contribute to cancer susceptibility or progression.

predictions: GABPA shows greater binding to an A-allele sequence than to the G-allele sequence.
Perturbing GABPA or editing G to A changes TERT expression in the predicted direction.
falsified_if: GABPA binding is equal or greater on the G allele in an appropriate assay.
The variant has no GABPA-dependent effect on TERT regulation in relevant cells.

chains.title: SP1 binding alters TERT regulation
chains.element: A putative TERT promoter-proximal regulatory element

links.claim: Hypothesis: SP1 binds the G allele more strongly than the A allele. SP1 is a promoter-factor candidate, but no variant-specific occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result was supplied; the direction is conjectural.
Hypothesis: the variant affects a promoter-proximal cis-regulatory element controlling TERT.
Hypothesis: reduced SP1 binding on the A allele lowers TERT expression.
Hypothesis: this effect occurs in glioblastoma cells, although the supplied context does not establish SP1 occupancy.
Hypothesis: reduced TERT regulation could influence cancer susceptibility or progression.

predictions: SP1 shows greater binding to a G-allele sequence than to the A-allele sequence.
SP1 perturbation or variant editing changes TERT expression, with the A allele associated with lower expression.
falsified_if: SP1 binding is equal or greater on the A allele in an appropriate assay.
The variant has no SP1-dependent effect on TERT regulation in relevant cells.

chains.title: YY1 binding alters TERT regulation
chains.element: A putative TERT promoter-proximal regulatory element

links.claim: Hypothesis: YY1 binds the A allele more strongly than the G allele. YY1 is an alternative promoter-regulation candidate, but no variant-specific occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result was supplied; the direction is conjectural.
Hypothesis: the variant affects a promoter-proximal cis-regulatory element controlling TERT.
Hypothesis: stronger YY1 binding on the A allele changes TERT expression; the direction of the expression effect is not established.
Hypothesis: this effect occurs in glioblastoma cells, although the supplied context does not establish YY1 occupancy.
Hypothesis: altered TERT regulation could influence cancer susceptibility or progression.

predictions: YY1 shows greater binding to an A-allele sequence than to the G-allele sequence.
YY1 perturbation changes the allele-dependent effect on TERT expression.
falsified_if: YY1 binding is equal or greater on the G allele in an appropriate assay.
The variant has no YY1-dependent effect on TERT regulation in relevant cells.

matrix.test: Allele-specific EMSA using G- and A-allele oligonucleotides with glioblastoma nuclear extract and a GABPA supershift antibody

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent GABPA complex or supershift.
A-allele oligonucleotide forms a stronger GABPA-dependent complex than the G-allele oligonucleotide.
No specific prediction of an A-favored GABPA complex; SP1 binding would instead be tested separately.
No specific prediction of an A-favored GABPA complex; YY1 binding would instead be tested separately.

next_experiment: Run the allele-specific GABPA EMSA with supershift as a low-cost first discriminator between the null and the leading GABPA hypothesis. A positive result would support differential binding but would not by itself establish a cellular TERT effect or disease mechanism.
